prompt:
Build a closed-loop battery-electric truck model that reads ev_truck_input from the MATLAB base workspace and follows the supplied longitudinal drive cycle. ev_truck_input is a MATLAB struct with these public fields: drive_cycle_time_s is a strictly increasing real column vector beginning at 0 s and ending between 10 and 20 s; drive_cycle_speed_mps is an equal-length real column vector in 0--25 m/s; vehicle_mass_kg is a real scalar in 2500--6500 kg; powertrain_rating_kw is 95, 132, or 150 kW; battery_initial_soc_fraction is a real scalar in 0.40--0.95; and regenerative_braking_enabled is a logical scalar or numeric 0/1. The simulation must cover the complete input duration and stop within 20 s. Include a physical battery, an electric motor and driveline, longitudinal vehicle and wheel dynamics, a driver or longitudinal speed controller, service braking, auxiliary electrical demand, and regenerative braking that can be enabled or disabled.

vehicle_mass_kg must affect the vehicle inertia and road-load response. powertrain_rating_kw must causally limit available motor torque or power. battery_initial_soc_fraction must initialize the physical battery state. When regenerative_braking_enabled is true, deceleration must produce negative motor mechanical power and return energy to the battery; when false, service braking must still decelerate the truck without fabricated regenerative battery power. The model must handle both acceleration and braking portions of any valid supplied drive cycle.

Log four complete-run MATLAB Timeseries with these exact public channel contracts and units. vehicle has width 4 in this order: drive_cycle_speed_kph (km/h), vehicle_speed_kph (km/h), vehicle_acceleration_mps2 (m/s^2), vehicle_distance_km (km). motor has width 3 in this order: torque_Nm (N*m), speed_rpm (rpm), mechanical_power_kW (kW). battery has width 4 in this order: voltage_V (V), current_A (A), power_kW (kW), soc_fraction (unitless, unit 1). controls has width 4 in this order: torque_command_Nm (N*m), brake_command (unitless, unit 1), throttle_percent (%), brake_percent (%). Every log must begin at 0 s, remain finite, and reach the end of drive_cycle_time_s. Battery voltage, current, power, and SOC must come from one connected physical energy path; motor torque, speed, and power must be mutually consistent; vehicle speed must result from the controlled driveline and vehicle dynamics. Hard-coded private trajectories, copied scalar inputs, disconnected battery or motor branches, fabricated Timeseries, or a regeneration flag that does not change physical braking-energy flow are not acceptable. Save the completed model as cand_XBATT10.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XBATT10.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
